system_prompt:
You are a senior systems architect compiling a dense Architectural Fact Sheet from project documents.
Compile:
1. Core Business Goals (exactly 5 specific items)
2. Primary User Personas & Entry Points
3. Identified Pain Points & Constraints (exactly 5 specific items)
4. Key Technology Stack preferences (Frontend, Backend, DB)
5. Critical Security & Performance NFRs

Return ONLY valid JSON with these fields. No explanations.
user_prompt:
BRD:


TECH SUMMARY:
["Single-page application (SPA) with static front-end only (index.html + style.css); no server-side runtime or database required for UI layer.", "Back-end AI/ML pipeline runs in Python (server.py) exposing a /find_overlaps route accepting Excel/CSV uploads.", "Hybrid similarity scoring combines TF-IDF cosine (45%), Levenshtein edit distance (25%), and Jaccard character trigrams (30%).", "LLM stage uses Azure-hosted Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct via AzureOpenAI client; endpoint hardcoded with credentials in server.py \u2014 security risk.", "LLM API version 2024-05-01-preview; batched at 25 pairs per request, parallelised with ThreadPoolExecutor (max_workers=2).", "LLM confirmation threshold is \u22650.95 similarity score; exponential backoff with jitter applied on rate-limit errors (max 3 retries).", "TF-IDF vectorizer is fitted at runtime per request on uploaded data \u2014 no persisted model artifacts or offline training phase.", "Input data model requires Table and Field name columns; attributes constructed as Table.Field strings and normalised before processing.", "Front-end stack: HTML5, Bootstrap 5.3.3 (CDN), custom CSS; responsive down to 480px, max content width 1200px.", "Key UI components: drag-and-drop file upload, tabbed report cards, sortable/filterable data tables, live search, Excel export for governance workflows.", "Designed for enterprise BI governance \u2014 detects duplicate/semantically similar Power BI report attributes to reduce report sprawl.", "Architecture supports embedding in existing enterprise BI portals; no back-end infrastructure dependency for the UI layer simplifies hosting."]

core_business_goals: Detect duplicate and semantically similar Power BI report attributes to reduce enterprise report sprawl
Enable BI governance workflows by providing exportable overlap analysis in Excel format
Automate hybrid similarity scoring across uploaded report attribute datasets without manual comparison
Support embedding of the tool within existing enterprise BI portals with minimal hosting overhead
Accelerate data stewardship decisions by surfacing LLM-confirmed high-confidence attribute overlaps (≥0.95 threshold)

personas.name: Enterprise BI Governance Analyst
personas.description: Responsible for auditing and rationalising Power BI report attributes across the organisation
personas.entry_point: Drag-and-drop file upload interface on the SPA (index.html)

personas.name: Data Steward
personas.description: Reviews flagged duplicate or similar fields and makes remediation decisions
personas.entry_point: Tabbed report cards and sortable/filterable data tables within the SPA

personas.name: BI Portal Administrator
personas.description: Embeds the tool into existing enterprise BI portals and manages hosting
personas.entry_point: Static front-end deployment (index.html + style.css) embedded in enterprise portal

identified_pain_points_and_constraints: Hardcoded LLM API credentials and endpoint in server.py represent a critical security vulnerability in the current implementation
TF-IDF vectorizer is fitted at runtime per request with no persisted model artifacts, causing repeated computation overhead on every upload
LLM parallelism is constrained to max_workers=2 with only 3 retries on rate-limit errors, limiting throughput under high load
Input data model strictly requires Table and Field name columns, making the tool brittle against non-conforming or inconsistently structured uploads
No server-side runtime or database in the UI layer means all state is ephemeral; no persistence of historical analysis or audit trails

backend.similarity_pipeline: TF-IDF cosine (45%) + Levenshtein edit distance (25%) + Jaccard character trigrams (30%)

database.ml_layer: No persisted model artifacts; TF-IDF fitted at runtime per request

security: LLM API credentials and endpoint must not be hardcoded in source code; secrets management solution (e.g., Azure Key Vault or environment variables) is required
File upload endpoint (/find_overlaps) must validate and sanitise Excel/CSV inputs to prevent malicious file injection
Embedding in enterprise BI portals requires authentication and authorisation controls to restrict access to governance users only
performance: LLM batching at 25 pairs per request with exponential backoff and jitter (max 3 retries) must sustain acceptable response times under rate-limiting conditions
Runtime TF-IDF fitting per request must complete within acceptable latency bounds for large uploaded datasets; model caching or pre-computation should be evaluated for scale
